domain: English tower-bell change ringing (campanology): place notation and the blue line, the method/call distinction, Central Council rules refusing rotations and renamings of methods already in the collection, truth as no-repeated-row, false course ends proved before ringing, practice nights as the currency of a method's cost, the weakest-ringer constraint, band size as topology, and the periodic withdrawal of duplicate methods
axioms: A method changes what every participant does on every row; a call redirects an unchanged method. Conflating the two is the characteristic error, and the cure is to demand the place notation.
A proposal that is a rotation, reversal, or renaming of something already in the collection is refused by construction, not weighed on its merits.
Redundancy is falseness, not inefficiency: one proved repeated row ends a distinctness claim without a cost-benefit argument.
Truth is provable in advance from the composition (false course ends), so verification precedes any performance.
The cost of a method is denominated in practice nights - what humans must learn and hold - not in the labour of writing it down.
A tower can only ring what its weakest available ringer has learned; operability is set by the weakest participant under load, not the strongest.
Adding a bell rewrites every other ringer's line; no addition is local.
The plain course is the honest null, and calling nothing is a respectable outcome.
primitives: call (Bob, Single) and the caller's vocabulary size
plain course, touch, quarter-peal, extent (budget lengths)
band size and the weakest-ringer constraint
striking quality and ropesight (execution under load)
the method collection, admission, renaming, decommissioning
failure_mode: Systematically under-values operations that are genuinely new but ugly or hard to name, because its admission test rewards learnable, well-formed lines and treats mnemonic awkwardness as evidence of non-distinctness.
Assumes a fixed repertoire and a governing collection, so it is weak on candidates whose value is emergent or discovered only in use rather than provable in advance.

Its truth test is combinatorial and structural, so it can miss a real difference that shows up only in outcomes - two candidates ringing the same rows for different reasons, with different downstream effects, look identical to it.
Biased toward 'a call, not a method' and toward the plain course, so it will under-detect the rare case where a genuine seventh phase is warranted.
Prices human learning cost well and machine/implementation cost badly; runtime, storage, latency, and code-maintenance considerations are invisible to it.
Assumes participants are cooperative, co-located, and synchronised in a fixed circle, so asynchronous, adversarial, or dynamically-sized multi-agent topologies fall outside its intuitions.
